Full name: **Black kippah from the house of Szymon Kluger in Oświęcim, Poland**

Known as a kippah or a yarmulke, it seems to be the most universally recognised symbol of Jewish religiosity and culture.  What is the origin of the custom of wearing this small brimless skullcap by Jewish men atop their head? The practice of covering only the crown of one’s head is not rooted in any Biblical or Talmudic precepts. Instead, its foundation lies in the description of the clothes of a high priest (Exodus 28:4, 36-39) or in the traditional headwear of Talmudic scholars in Babylonia.

candidates.source_description:
Statuette of a lion, 11th-12th C CE, now in the collection of the Minneapolis Institute of Art.


From the object's description on [artsmia.org](https://artsmia.org/): 



*"This rare and enigmatic gold sculpture of a lion—a symbol of power and authority—is elaborately decorated with looping filigree and fine granulation, in keeping with the Islamic goldsmithing traditions of the later Muslim kingdoms of the Iberian Peninsula (present-day Spain and Portugal). Islam arrived in Europe in 711 CE, bringing new traditions in the decorative arts, such as the animal-shaped aquamanile: a vessel used for hand washing, which the Qur’an requires before prayer. The work closest in size, style, and workmanship to this lion is a winged ram found in northwestern Spain, leading us to believe that this work, too, is from Muslim Spain."*

More information [here](https://collections.artsmia.org/art/19884/statuette-of-a-lion-unknown)


Model building and customization for Mia by [Lou Brown](https://www.artstation.com/loubrown)

Sinan Pasha Mosque in Prizren
The Sinan Pasha Mosque, located in the historic town of Prizren, Kosovo, is a remarkable example of Ottoman architecture. Built in 1615 by Sofi Sinan Pasha, a high-ranking Ottoman official, the mosque stands as a testament to the region's rich cultural and religious history. Its large, single dome, ornate mihrab (prayer niche), and finely detailed minaret are characteristic features of Ottoman mosque design.The mosque's interior is adorned with intricate floral and geometric patterns, along with calligraphic inscriptions from the Quran. The exterior, constructed primarily from finely cut stone, reflects the grandeur typical of Ottoman-era public buildings. The mosque's central location in Prizren makes it not only a place of worship but also a significant cultural landmark, drawing visitors interested in its historical and architectural beauty. 
To create a 3D model of the Mosque, I used Lumelabs AI and drone video of 360° view of the Mosque.

Sobre su cabeza lleva un kalathos cónico y liso y las orejas aparecen con el lóbulo inferior perforado para llevar aretes. Conserva todavía restos de engobe blanquecino y policromía en tono rojizo por el cabello y los labios. Esta figura tiene sus prototipos en la isla de Sicilia, de donde con toda probabilidad procede dada su composicón cerámica. Se pueden encontrar paralelos próximos o muy similares entre la coroplastia sicilota y de la Magna Grecia de principios o mediados del siglo IV a C. Esta terracota que en origen con toda probabilidad representaba a la diosa Demeter, su hallazgo en Ibiza hace que se pueda vincular con las divinidades locales y pueda ser asimilada con la diosa cartaginesa Tanit
